paragraphs: i-Probe monitors road conditions with connected vehicles, which the pages define as vehicles that use bidirectional communications to address road conditions, safety, system efficiency, or mobility on roadways. The pages address road management agencies and describe the offering as more economical, rapid, and consistent road condition monitoring. The technology leverages factory-installed sensors already built into later-model production vehicles, developed in partnership with Honda Motors, and requires no aftermarket equipment.

Connected vehicles collect road roughness data either through crowdsourcing or through a single-vehicle service. That roughness data is processed under an i-Probe algorithm to identify pavement distresses and severity, and the outputs are mapped and tabulated in a cloud dashboard. Distress identification and classification are automated and paired with video verification. Reasons given for choosing the service include results correlated to IRI. Wide-area monitoring of an entire road network is listed among those reasons.
The page names county and municipal public works agencies as one group served. Pavement maintenance service providers are named as the other group served.

quote.text: Transforming road management with continuous road condition data.
